text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Thursday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Two strategic investors of Latvian Gas, Gazprom and Preussen/Ruhrgas, signed an agreement on buying 32.5 percent of the company's stock.
- The Bank of Latvia decided that the licence of Sakaru Banka should be cancelled beginning April 3, since it failed to bring its capital to one million lats.
- The Bank of Latvia announced the profit of the country's 27 commercial banks last year totalled 33 million lats. Five banks were in the red with losses of six million lats.
- Prime Minister Andris Shkele believes Minister of Economics Guntars Krasts should not interfere with the process of choosing the directors of the privatisation agency.

- While meeting editors of the local press, President Guntis Ulmanis issued a statement calling for the scrapping of the age limits in the law on non-citizens, mainly Russian-speakers, becoming Latvian citizens. The law allows people to apply to be naturalised according to their age.
- The ministry of justice warned seven political parties, including two parliamentary ones, that their activities could be stopped if they failed to file financial declarations.

- Next week Prime Minister Shkele and Interior Minister Dainis Turlais will visit Sweden to sign agreement on the re-admission of illegal immigrants. They will also have talks with Swedish Prime Minister Goran Persson.
- Repshe announced that the level of inflation in the country has for the first time dropped below 9.9 percent. Nevertheless, he doubted the ability to keep the inflation so low throughout the year.
- The state traumatology hospital may be cut off from the heating supply because of a failure to pay its energy debts.
- Shkele announced that the government will allow the monopoly of Lattelekom until 2003 at the latest.
- Foreign Minister Valdis Birkavs is planning to go on a cenral Asia tour later this month.
- The last year's profit of Rietumu Banka, Latvia's fourth largest bank, was 4.58 million lats. The assets of the bank have increased 42.9 million lats to 88.2 million lats.
